spots.name: Mayon Volcano
spots.short: The world's most perfect volcanic cone — visible from the boulevard, the riles, the SM road, everywhere.
spots.description: You don't go to Mayon — Mayon comes to you. The volcano is present in almost every shot across the city: rising at the end of East Washington Drive, looming over the boulevard at dusk, glimpsed down every open road. Capture it in as many natural contexts as possible.

spots.name: Centrong Albay
spots.short: The civic heart of Legazpi — Peñaranda Park, the old city hall, and the streets that tie it all together.
spots.description: Centro Albay is where the city's public life has always centered. Peñaranda Park anchors the area — surrounded by the old city hall, heritage buildings, and the everyday rhythm of Legazpi's downtown. A place worth slowing down in.

spots.name: Artisans & Pasalubong Stores
spots.short: Pili candy, abaca crafts, local art — Bicol's best take-homes, including Initial Arts at SM.
spots.description: Legazpi's pasalubong culture is worth documenting — the local stores lined with pili nut sweets, abaca weavings, and regional handicrafts. Initial Arts inside SM Legazpi is a standout. A quick walk-through and a few product shots capture the full picture.

spots.name: Lapu-Lapu Street
spots.assigned: Frederick B. Baldano & Rein Allen M. Capitulo
spots.short: The real Legazpi — narrow eskinitas, the Ibalong Monument, and the Battle of Legazpi Monument.
spots.description: Brgy 25 Lapu-Lapu Street is everyday Legazpi at full volume. Narrow eskinitas cutting between buildings, the Ibalong Monument and Battle of Legazpi Monument anchoring the area with history that most visitors never find.

spots.name: Kawit, East Washington Drive
spots.short: Where the old railway line meets the bay - Legazpi's most atmospheric bayside stretch.
spots.description: East Washington Drive runs along the Legazpi bay front through Brgy 16 Kawit, tracing the old PNR Bicol railway corridor. The riles are quiet now, but the energy of the place hasn't left — fishermen, open water, Mayon at the end of the gulf. Best at sunrise or sundown.

spots.name: Pawa
spots.short: A quiet barangay on the slopes. Rice fields, open views of Mayon, and a pace that feels genuinely unhurried.
spots.description: Pawa is one of those barangays that rewards the detour. Situated away from the city bustle, it offers open views toward Mayon, terraced landscapes, and a daily rhythm that contrasts sharply with downtown Legazpi. A good stop for anyone wanting the quieter side of the city.

spots.name: Embarcadero Boulevard</br>& Sawangan Park
spots.short: A scenic waterfront destination where locals and visitors gather to enjoy the sea breeze, relaxing sunsets, and clear views of Mayon Volcano. The boulevard is perfect for evening walks, food trips, and casual hangouts by the bay.
spots.description: Something about the park and its one of the city's best place to spend along with open bay views, the volcano catching the last light, vendors along the promenade. A perfect end to a day anywhere in the city.

spots.name: Obelisk
spots.short: Located along the baywalk, the Obelisk area offers one of the best urban views of Mayon Volcano, especially during golden hour.
spots.description: From Embarcadero de Legazpi along the boulevard to Sawangan and upto Obelisk is one of the city's best evening walks. It’s a lively roadside stop known for its coastal atmosphere, nearby food stalls, and relaxing seaside vibe.

spots.name: Liñon Hill
spots.short: A hilltop viewpoint perfect for jogging, sightseeing, and panoramic city views. It is also one of the best spots in Legazpi to admire the beauty of Mayon Volcano.
spots.description: A popular hilltop destination known for its panoramic view of Mayon Volcano and Legazpi City. Lignon Hill is ideal for jogging, sightseeing, and outdoor activities, offering fresh air, greenery, and one of the city’s most iconic viewpoints.

food.name: Bicol Express
food.description: Pork slow-cooked in coconut milk with an avalanche of labuyo chili. Fiery, creamy, deeply savory. The dish that put Bicol on the map.

food.name: Gulay na Natong
food.description: Gabi (taro) leaves and stalks cooked down in rich coconut cream with bagoong. Humble, earthy, and one of the most distinctly Bicolano dishes you'll find.

food.name: Laing
food.description: Dried taro leaves simmered in coconut cream with shrimp paste and chili until thick and deeply flavored. Deceptively simple, impossibly good.

food.name: Pili Nuts & Sweets
food.description: Bicol's prized nut — candied, salted, in pastillas, or pressed into oil. Every pasalubong store in the city carries them. Don't leave without some.
food.where: Pasalubong stores, SM Legazpi, Initial Arts

food.name: Hepa Streets Food Park
food.description: A lively stretch of food stalls and local vendors operating side by side. Good for an evening out — affordable, casual, and very Legazpi.
